articles.title: About FleetNimble
articles.answer: FleetNimble is a comprehensive fleet management platform that gives you real-time GPS tracking, live OBD-II diagnostics, digital twin modeling, driver behavior analytics, fuel management, and AI-powered insights — all in one dashboard. We help fleet operators reduce costs, improve safety, and maximize vehicle uptime.
articles.details: FleetNimble was founded to solve the fragmentation problem in fleet management — operators having to use separate tools for GPS tracking, diagnostics, maintenance, fuel, and driver management. Our platform unifies all these capabilities under a single dashboard with AI-driven insights. We serve fleets of all sizes from small businesses with 5 vehicles to enterprise fleets with 1000+ vehicles across logistics, transportation, construction, and field service industries.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Many of our customers start with GPS tracking and live diagnostics, then add digital twin and AI analytics as they see the value. Would you like to hear about our complete platform?

articles.title: Fleet Management Overview
articles.answer: FleetNimble gives you a single dashboard to manage your entire fleet — vehicle tracking, live diagnostics, maintenance schedules, driver performance, fuel consumption, and AI-powered reports. Everything is real-time and accessible from any device.
articles.details: The FleetNimble platform is organized into core modules accessible from the sidebar: Dashboard (real-time fleet overview), Vehicles (per-vehicle detail), GPS Tracking (live map), Diagnostics (OBD-II live data), Maintenance (schedules and history), Fuel Analytics, Driver Management, Alerts, Reports, AI Assistant, and AI Receptionist. Each module pulls real-time telemetry from connected vehicles via OBD-II devices and presents actionable insights.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: The Fleet Management Dashboard is where it all comes together. Without leaving that screen, you can see which vehicles need maintenance, which drivers need coaching, and where your fleet is right now.

articles.title: Dashboard
articles.answer: The FleetNimble Dashboard gives you a real-time overview of your entire fleet. You can see vehicle status — online or offline — active alerts, fuel levels, GPS positions, live diagnostics data, and key performance metrics. Vehicle cards are color-coded: green for online, red for offline, and yellow for idling.
articles.details: The Dashboard is the first screen you see after login. It is designed for at-a-glance fleet awareness. Key widgets include: Fleet Status (count of online/offline/idle vehicles), Active Alerts (critical and high-severity alerts requiring attention), Fuel Overview (current fuel levels and consumption trends), GPS Map Snapshot (last known positions), Maintenance Due (upcoming service tasks), Driver Score Summary, and Quick Actions (add vehicle, create report, open AI Assistant). Data refreshes automatically every 30 seconds when vehicles are transmitting telemetry.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: The Dashboard widgets are customizable. Many fleet managers set it up as their command center and never need to drill into individual pages except for detailed analysis.

articles.title: Vehicle Detail Page
articles.answer: The Vehicles page lists every vehicle in your fleet. Each vehicle card shows the name, VIN, plate number, status, last GPS position, and key live metrics. Click into any vehicle to see live diagnostics, GPS tracking history, trips, maintenance records, DTC fault codes, and driver assignments.
articles.details: From the Vehicles page (sidebar > Vehicles), you can search, filter by status (online/offline/idle/maintenance), group by fleet category, and bulk-assign drivers. The vehicle detail page is organized into tabs: Overview (key stats and status), Live Diagnostics (real-time OBD-II data stream), GPS Tracking (location history and playback), Trips (all trip records with routes, distance, duration, fuel used), Maintenance (scheduled and completed tasks), DTC Codes (diagnostic trouble codes and clear actions), Driver (assigned driver and performance score), and Telemetry (raw sensor data feed).
articles.proactiveSalesTip: The vehicle detail page is where our Digital Twin feature really shines — it creates a real-time virtual copy of each vehicle that mirrors its actual sensor data.

articles.title: GPS Tracking
articles.answer: GPS Tracking shows all your vehicles on a live map with real-time positions. Each vehicle displays speed, heading, ignition status, and last update time. You can filter by vehicle, view historical playback, and set up geofence boundaries with instant alerts.
articles.details: The GPS Tracking page (sidebar > GPS Tracking) uses a dynamic map interface (Google Maps or OpenStreetMap). Key features: Live position updates every 5-30 seconds depending on telemetry frequency, vehicle clustering at zoom levels, color-coded markers by status (green = moving, blue = idle, red = stopped/offline), speed and heading indicators, geofence management (create circular or polygonal zones with custom alert triggers), historical playback (replay any vehicle route for a selected date range with speed visualization), trip detection (automatic trip start/end based on ignition), and address reverse-geocoding for last known location. GPS data is sourced from the connected OBD-II device's onboard GPS or an external GPS tracker.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: GPS Tracking becomes even more powerful when combined with Live Diagnostics — you can see not just where a vehicle is, but how it's performing in real time.

articles.title: Geofence Management
articles.answer: Geofences let you set up virtual boundaries on the map. When a vehicle enters or leaves a geofence, you receive an instant alert. You can create circular or custom-shaped zones and assign them to specific vehicles or groups.
articles.details: Geofences are managed from GPS Tracking > Geofences tab. You can create circular zones (center point + radius in meters) or polygonal zones (draw custom shape on map). Each geofence can trigger alerts on Entry, Exit, or Both. Alerts can be routed to specific users or groups. Use cases include: unauthorized vehicle use (nighttime movement alerts), arrival/departure notifications for job sites, speed restriction zones, and no-go area enforcement. Geofences can be temporarily enabled or disabled without deletion.

articles.title: Trip History & Playback
articles.answer: Trip History records every journey your vehicles make. You can replay any trip on the map, see distance, duration, fuel used, average speed, max speed, and driving events like harsh braking or rapid acceleration.
articles.details: Trips are automatically detected based on ignition status (ignition on = trip start, ignition off = trip end). Each trip record includes: start and end timestamps, start and end locations (reverse-geocoded addresses), total distance in km/miles, duration, fuel consumption estimate, average and max speed, idle time, driving events (harsh braking, rapid acceleration, cornering), and GPS route path (polyline for map playback). Trip playback animates the vehicle along the route path with speed color-coding. Trips can be exported as CSV or PDF. Filters available by vehicle, date range, driver, and minimum distance.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Trip data feeds directly into driver scorecards — making it easy to identify coaching opportunities and reward safe driving.

articles.title: Live Diagnostics
articles.answer: Live Diagnostics shows real-time OBD-II data from your connected vehicles. You can see RPM, speed, coolant temperature, battery voltage, fuel level, engine load, throttle position, intake temperature, MAF, ignition status, and active DTC codes. Data streams live while the engine is running.
articles.details: Live Diagnostics is accessible from the vehicle detail page (Vehicles > Select Vehicle > Live Diagnostics tab) or from the Diagnostics page in the sidebar. The interface shows gauges and numeric readouts that update in real time (typically every 1-3 seconds when connected). Supported PIDs include: Engine RPM, Vehicle Speed (km/h), Coolant Temperature, Fuel Level (%), Battery Voltage, Engine Load (%), Throttle Position, Intake Air Temperature, Mass Air Flow (MAF), Calculated Engine Load, Timing Advance, Fuel Pressure, Intake Manifold Pressure, O2 Sensor voltages, Ignition Status (on/off), and Check Engine Light status. Historical diagnostic data is stored and can be graphed over time. If a vehicle is offline, the last known readings are displayed with a timestamp.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Live Diagnostics data feeds directly into our predictive maintenance engine — helping you catch issues before they become breakdowns.

articles.title: DTC Fault Codes
articles.answer: FleetNimble reads and displays Diagnostic Trouble Codes from your vehicles. Each DTC shows the code, description, severity, and when it was first detected. You can clear codes after repairs and view the full history of resolved and active faults.
articles.details: DTC codes are displayed on the vehicle detail page under the DTC Codes tab. Codes are categorized by severity: Critical (immediate attention required — e.g., engine misfire, catalyst damage), High (should be addressed soon — e.g., oxygen sensor, EGR), Medium (monitor and schedule repair), and Low (informational). Each code includes: the standard 5-character code (e.g., P0301), manufacturer-specific code if applicable, human-readable description, date first detected, date last seen, occurrence count, and related freeze frame data (RPM, speed, coolant temp at time of code). You can generate a DTC report, clear codes (with confirmation), and set up automatic alerts for specific DTC codes.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Setting up automatic alerts for specific DTC codes means you never miss a critical engine fault — even when your team is on the road.

articles.title: Connecting an OBD-II Device
articles.answer: To connect an OBD-II device, go to Vehicles, select your vehicle, and click Connect OBD. FleetNimble supports ELM327 Bluetooth OBD adapters and the FleetNimble OBD Gateway. Pair the device via Bluetooth first in your device settings, then select it in the app. Once connected, you will see live diagnostics data, DTC codes, and telemetry streaming in real time.
articles.details: Supported OBD-II devices: Standard ELM327 Bluetooth adapters (compatible with most vehicles manufactured after 1996 in the US, 2001 in EU, 2003 in Asia), FleetNimble OBD Gateway (recommended — provides wider PID support, better sample rate, and integrated GPS). Connection steps: 1) Insert OBD device into vehicle's OBD-II port (usually under dashboard near steering column), 2) Turn vehicle ignition to ON position (engine may need to be running for live data), 3) Enable Bluetooth on the smartphone or tablet running FleetNimble, 4) Go to Vehicles > Select Vehicle > Connect OBD, 5) Select the device from the list, 6) Wait for connection confirmation. Troubleshooting: ensure device is not paired to another phone, check Bluetooth range (within 5 meters), verify vehicle compatibility, try restarting the app. Connection status is shown on the vehicle detail page with a green (connected), yellow (connecting), or red (disconnected) indicator.

articles.title: FleetNimble OBD Gateway
articles.answer: The FleetNimble OBD Gateway is our recommended hardware adapter. It provides faster data sampling, broader PID support, built-in GPS, and cellular connectivity so your vehicle stays connected even without a phone nearby. Contact our sales team for pricing.
articles.details: The FleetNimble OBD Gateway is a purpose-built OBD-II adapter designed for commercial fleet use. Key advantages over generic ELM327 adapters: 10x faster data sampling rate (50ms vs 500ms), wider PID coverage (reads manufacturer-specific PIDs), integrated GPS module for accurate positioning, cellular modem (4G LTE) for independent connectivity, extended Bluetooth range (30m), ruggedized design for commercial vehicles, OTA firmware updates, and FleetNimble cloud integration out of the box. The Gateway can store telemetry data locally when out of cellular range and sync when connectivity is restored.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: The OBD Gateway is what enables our most advanced features — Digital Twin, predictive maintenance, and real-time telemetry even when the driver's phone is off.

articles.title: OBD Connection Troubleshooting
articles.answer: If your OBD device is not connecting, try these steps: 1) Make sure the vehicle ignition is on, 2) Check that Bluetooth is enabled on your device, 3) Ensure the OBD adapter is not paired to another phone, 4) Restart the FleetNimble app, 5) Remove and reinsert the OBD adapter. If the issue continues, I can create a support ticket for our technical team.
articles.details: Common OBD connection issues and solutions: No Bluetooth device found — ensure OBD adapter has power (LED should be lit), try removing and reinserting into OBD port, check vehicle compatibility. Device paired but no data — vehicle may not support the requested PIDs, try turning ignition off and on, ensure the app has location permission (required for Bluetooth scanning on Android 12+). Connection drops frequently — Bluetooth range exceeded, low adapter battery (some adapters have internal batteries), interference from other Bluetooth devices, try moving phone closer to OBD port. No GPS signal — vehicle may be in a parking garage or tunnel, move to open sky, check if OBD Gateway has cellular signal. For persistent issues, create a support ticket and include vehicle make, model, year, OBD adapter model, and phone model.

articles.title: Digital Twin
articles.answer: The Digital Twin creates a real-time virtual copy of each vehicle that mirrors its actual sensor data, diagnostics, GPS position, and operational status. It combines live telemetry with historical patterns to give you a complete digital representation of your physical fleet.
articles.details: The Digital Twin feature (accessible from the vehicle detail page > Digital Twin tab) provides a 3D or schematic representation of each vehicle with overlaid real-time data. Components visualized include: engine (RPM, load, temperature), transmission, battery/electrical system, fuel system, cooling system, exhaust/emissions, braking system, tires (via TPMS integration), and GPS location. The Digital Twin updates in real time with incoming telemetry and can replay historical states. Advanced features include: predictive analytics (wear estimation, failure probability), simulation (what-if scenarios for maintenance or route changes), and anomaly detection (flags unusual sensor readings compared to the vehicle's own history). Digital Twin data feeds into the AI Assistant for natural language queries about vehicle health.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Digital Twin is especially powerful for preventive maintenance. It can predict component wear before failure — saving you from costly roadside breakdowns.

articles.title: Predictive Maintenance
articles.answer: Predictive Maintenance uses your vehicle's live diagnostic data and history to forecast when components are likely to fail or need service. It helps you schedule maintenance proactively instead of reacting to breakdowns.
articles.details: FleetNimble's predictive maintenance engine analyzes telemetry patterns including: engine load history, temperature cycles, RPM ranges, idle time ratios, vibration data (if available), DTC frequency, and maintenance interval compliance. It predicts remaining useful life for key components and assigns a health score (0-100%) per vehicle. When a component's predicted failure window approaches, the system generates a maintenance alert with the estimated time-to-service. This is accessible from the Maintenance page or the Digital Twin tab. Predictive models improve over time as more vehicle data is collected.

articles.title: Maintenance Management
articles.answer: The Maintenance page shows all maintenance schedules and service history for your fleet. You can set up recurring tasks like oil changes, tire rotations, brake inspections, and timing belt replacements. Each task tracks due dates, mileage intervals, and completion status.
articles.details: Maintenance Management (sidebar > Maintenance) is organized into: Upcoming Maintenance (tasks due or overdue within the next 30 days), All Schedules (all recurring and one-time maintenance plans), Service History (completed tasks with dates, costs, and notes), and Vehicle View (per-vehicle maintenance timeline). Each maintenance task includes: task name, assigned vehicle, interval type (time-based, mileage-based, or both), interval value (e.g., 6 months or 10,000 km), last completed date and mileage, next due date and mileage, assigned vendor or technician, estimated cost, priority, and notes. You can mark tasks as completed, reschedule, assign to vendors, and generate maintenance reports. Automatic alerts are sent when tasks are due, overdue, or approaching the interval threshold.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Combine scheduled maintenance with our predictive analytics and you'll always know which vehicle needs attention before it fails.

articles.title: Fuel Analytics
articles.answer: Fuel Analytics shows fuel consumption trends, efficiency metrics, and cost analysis for your fleet. You can view fuel usage per vehicle, compare efficiency across your fleet, track fuel costs over time, and identify anomalies like excessive idling or potential fuel theft.
articles.details: Fuel Analytics (sidebar > Fuel) sources data from OBD-II telemetry (fuel level, fuel rate, MAF sensor) and manual fuel log entries. Key metrics: Fuel Consumption (liters/gallons per trip, day, week, month), Fuel Efficiency (km/l or MPG per vehicle, with fleet average comparison), Fuel Cost (total spend, cost per km/mile, cost trend), Idle Fuel Waste (estimated fuel consumed during idle time), Anomaly Detection (unusual consumption patterns that may indicate theft, leaks, or mechanical issues), and Carbon Footprint (CO2 emissions estimate). Data can be filtered by vehicle, date range, driver, and fleet group. Reports can be exported as CSV or PDF. Comparison charts show best and worst performing vehicles.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Fuel is typically the second-largest fleet expense after labor. Our customers typically reduce fuel costs by 8-15% within the first three months by identifying inefficiencies.

articles.title: Driver Management
articles.answer: The Drivers page lets you manage driver profiles and assign them to vehicles. Each driver has a performance scorecard based on behavior events like harsh braking, rapid acceleration, speeding, cornering, and idling. Scorecards help identify safe versus risky drivers.
articles.details: Driver Management (sidebar > Drivers) shows a list of all drivers with their assigned vehicle, score, status (active/inactive), and last active date. Each driver profile includes: personal details (name, contact, license info), assigned vehicle history, performance score (0-100), behavior event counts by type, trip history linked to the driver, and coaching notes. Driver scores are calculated from: harsh braking events, rapid acceleration events, harsh cornering, speeding incidents (duration and severity), excessive idling, seatbelt status (if supported), and fuel efficiency score. Scores can be used for driver ranking, incentive programs, and targeted coaching. Drivers can be grouped into teams or regions for comparative analysis.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Driver scorecards are a proven way to reduce accident rates. Our customers see an average 30% reduction in harsh driving events within 60 days of implementing scorecard-based coaching.

articles.title: Driver Behavior & Safety
articles.answer: FleetNimble automatically detects driving behavior events using OBD-II and GPS data. Events include harsh braking, rapid acceleration, speeding, harsh cornering, and excessive idling. Each event is recorded with the date, location, and severity so you can coach drivers effectively.
articles.details: Behavior events are detected in real time by analyzing telemetry data streams. Detection thresholds are configurable per fleet or per vehicle. Harsh Braking: triggered when deceleration exceeds threshold (default 7 km/h per second). Rapid Acceleration: triggered when acceleration exceeds threshold (default 8 km/h per second). Speeding: triggered when speed exceeds configurable limit for configurable duration. Harsh Cornering: triggered when lateral acceleration exceeds threshold (default 5 m/s squared). Excessive Idling: triggered when vehicle idles beyond configurable time limit (default 10 minutes). Each event record includes: timestamp, GPS coordinates, speed at time of event, severity score, and driver name (if assigned). Events appear in the Alerts page, driver scorecards, and trip details. Aggregated behavior reports show trends over time.

articles.title: Alerts & Notifications
articles.answer: The Alerts page shows all active and historical alerts for your fleet. Alerts cover speeding events, geofence breaches, engine faults, maintenance due, driver behavior events, and DTC codes. Each alert shows severity, timestamp, and the related vehicle. You can mark alerts as read or configure which alerts you receive.
articles.details: Alerts (sidebar > Alerts) are organized by severity: Critical (immediate attention required — engine failure, accident detection, fuel theft), High (address within 24 hours — DTC codes, geofence breach, unauthorized use), Medium (address within a week — maintenance due, low fuel, low battery), and Low (informational — driver behavior, route deviation). Each alert shows: type icon, severity badge, title, vehicle name, timestamp, location (if applicable), and status (new, read, resolved). Filters available by severity, type, vehicle, date range, and status. Alert rules are configurable from Settings > Alerts. You can choose which alert types to receive, set thresholds (e.g., speed limit, geofence boundary), and configure notification channels (in-app, email, SMS, push). Alert history is retained for 90 days.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Well-configured alerts turn your fleet management from reactive to proactive. Most of our customers start with 5-10 alert rules and expand as they discover new use cases.

articles.title: Reports & Analytics
articles.answer: The Reports page lets you generate and download fleet analytics reports. Available reports include fuel consumption analysis, trip summaries, maintenance history, driver performance, DTC fault reports, and fleet utilization. Reports can be exported as PDF or CSV for sharing with your team.
articles.details: Reports (sidebar > Reports) offers pre-built report templates and a custom report builder. Pre-built reports: Fuel Consumption Report (consumption, cost, efficiency by vehicle and date range), Trip Summary Report (total trips, distance, duration, fuel used per period), Maintenance History Report (completed and pending tasks with costs), Driver Performance Report (scorecard summary, event counts, trends), DTC Fault Report (active and historical fault codes with frequency analysis), Fleet Utilization Report (vehicle usage percentage, idle time, downtime analysis), Geofence Compliance Report (entry/exit events by zone), and Custom Report Builder (select metrics, dimensions, filters, and visualization type). Reports can be scheduled for automatic generation (daily, weekly, monthly) and emailed to selected recipients. Data retention for reports is configurable up to 2 years.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Scheduled reports save hours of manual work. Set up weekly fleet performance reports and they'll land in your inbox automatically every Monday morning.

articles.title: CRM & Customer Management
articles.answer: The CRM module tracks all your customer interactions including calls, appointments, support tickets, and lead status. Every interaction with the AI Receptionist is automatically recorded in the CRM, giving you a complete history of each customer relationship.
articles.details: The CRM module is integrated with the AI Receptionist. When a customer calls, the system automatically looks them up by phone number and presents their full history: previous calls, scheduled appointments, support tickets, notes, lead score, and sentiment history. CRM features: Customer List (searchable with filters by status, lead score, date range), Customer Profile (details, interaction history, notes, related appointments and tickets), Lead Scoring (automatic scoring based on fleet size, company, interaction intent, and engagement), Activity Timeline (chronological view of all customer interactions), and Export (customer data export as CSV). Lead statuses: New, Contacted, Qualified, Demo Scheduled, Negotiation, Won, Lost. AI Receptionist interactions automatically update lead scores.

articles.title: AI Assistant
articles.answer: The AI Assistant is FleetNimble's intelligent chat interface. You can ask it questions about your fleet in plain English — like 'Which vehicles need maintenance this month?' or 'Show me drivers with the lowest safety scores.' It has real-time access to your fleet data and can generate reports, check vehicle status, and provide maintenance recommendations.
articles.details: AI Assistant (sidebar > AI Assistant) is powered by FleetNimble's AI engine with real-time access to your fleet database and telemetry. Capabilities include: Natural Language Queries (ask questions about your fleet in plain English), Data Analysis (trend analysis, anomaly detection, comparative analysis across vehicles), Report Generation (create and export fleet reports on demand), Vehicle Status Checks (live health, diagnostics summary, DTC status for any vehicle), Maintenance Recommendations (upcoming tasks, predictive alerts, component health), Driver Coaching Suggestions (based on behavior event patterns), Fuel Efficiency Tips (based on driving patterns and vehicle health), and Multi-language Support. The AI Assistant learns from your fleet's data patterns over time and provides increasingly personalized recommendations.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: The AI Assistant is like having a fleet analyst on staff 24/7. Instead of digging through screens, just ask and get an instant answer.

articles.title: AI Receptionist
articles.answer: The AI Receptionist is a voice-first agent that handles incoming calls for your business. It speaks naturally with callers, books demonstrations, schedules appointments, creates support tickets, and answers FleetNimble product questions. It collects information one step at a time and confirms before taking any action.
articles.details: The AI Receptionist (accessible from sidebar > AI Receptionist or via your assigned FleetNimble phone number) handles calls 24/7. Key features: Natural Voice Conversation (uses Gemini Live or OpenAI Realtime for human-like speech), Caller Identification (looks up returning customers by phone number for personalized greetings), Appointment Scheduling (collects caller info step by step and books demos or meetings in the CRM), Support Ticket Creation (captures issue details and creates tickets with appropriate urgency), Product Knowledge (answers questions about FleetNimble features, pricing, and capabilities from the verified knowledge base), Proactive Sales (naturally mentions related features when appropriate), Multi-turn Memory (remembers caller details, topics discussed, and conversation state within a call), Human Handoff (transfers to a human team member when needed), and Call Analytics (records call summaries, sentiment, and outcomes). The AI Receptionist is configurable per tenant with business hours, greeting messages, and tool enablement.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: The AI Receptionist works 24/7 without breaks. Every missed call becomes a booked demo or a logged support ticket — you never lose a lead again.

articles.title: FleetNimble Pricing
articles.answer: FleetNimble offers flexible pricing plans based on your fleet size and feature needs. We have plans for small fleets under 10 vehicles, medium fleets with 10 to 50 vehicles, and enterprise fleets with over 50 vehicles. Each plan includes GPS tracking, live diagnostics, maintenance management, alerts, and analytics. Enterprise plans add API access, white-label options, and dedicated support. For a tailored quote, I can schedule a demo with our sales team.
articles.details: Pricing tiers: Starter (up to 10 vehicles) — core GPS tracking, basic diagnostics, maintenance schedules, email alerts, standard reports, and AI Assistant access. Professional (10-50 vehicles) — everything in Starter plus advanced diagnostics, driver management with scorecards, fuel analytics, custom report builder, geofences, API access, and priority support. Enterprise (50+ vehicles) — everything in Professional plus digital twin, predictive maintenance, white-label dashboard, dedicated account manager, custom integrations, on-premise deployment option, SLA guarantees, and AI Receptionist. All plans include 14-day free trial. Annual billing discounts available. No long-term contracts on monthly plans. Hardware (OBD devices) sold separately or available with hardware-included plans.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Many of our customers start with the Professional plan and add enterprise features as their fleet grows. I can help you find the right plan — would you like to schedule a quick consultation?

articles.title: Schedule a Demo
articles.answer: I can help you schedule a personalized demo of FleetNimble right now. I'll need your name, company name, fleet size, and a preferred date and time. Our product team will walk you through the platform, answer your questions, and show you how FleetNimble can help your fleet. Just share your details and I'll get it set up.
articles.details: Demo process: 1) Caller provides name, company, fleet size, and contact info, 2) AI Receptionist suggests available time slots or caller provides preferred date/time, 3) AI summarizes details and asks for confirmation, 4) Upon confirmation, the system creates an appointment in the CRM and sends calendar invites, 5) Confirmation SMS is sent to the caller's phone. Demo duration is typically 30 minutes but can be extended to 45 or 60 minutes. Demos can be focused on specific areas (GPS tracking, diagnostics, digital twin, AI features) or cover the full platform. The demo is conducted via video call with a product specialist who can answer technical questions.

articles.title: Creating a Support Ticket
articles.answer: I can create a support ticket for any issue you're experiencing. I'll need your name, a description of the issue, and the best way to reach you. You can also let me know the urgency level and which vehicle is affected. Our support team will follow up with you promptly.
articles.details: Support ticket process: 1) Caller describes the issue, 2) AI Receptionist collects caller name, issue description, contact info (phone or email), urgency level (low, medium, high, critical), and affected vehicle if applicable, 3) AI summarizes the ticket and asks for confirmation, 4) Upon confirmation, a support ticket is created in the system with status OPEN, 5) Admin notification is sent, 6) Confirmation SMS is sent to the caller, 7) Support team picks up the ticket and investigates. Ticket statuses: Open, In Progress, Waiting on Customer, Resolved, Closed. Urgency levels: Low (minor inconvenience, next business day), Medium (moderate impact, within 8 business hours), High (significant impact, within 4 business hours), Critical (system down or safety issue, immediate response). Response times are targets and may vary based on support plan.

articles.title: Integrations
articles.answer: FleetNimble offers a REST API and webhooks for integrating with your existing systems. You can connect with accounting software, ERP systems, dispatch platforms, HR systems, and custom applications. Enterprise plans include dedicated integration support.
articles.details: Integration options: REST API (full CRUD access to vehicles, drivers, trips, diagnostics, maintenance, fuel, and alerts data), Webhooks (real-time event notifications for alerts, trip events, DTC codes, and status changes), Zapier (connect with 2000+ apps without coding), CSV/Excel Import/Export (bulk data operations), and Custom Integrations (Enterprise plan — dedicated integration engineering support). Typical integrations include: Accounting (QuickBooks, Xero, FreshBooks for fuel cost and maintenance expense tracking), ERP (SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics for fleet asset management), Dispatch (Route4Me, Onfleet, Bringg for trip and job linking), HR/Payroll (ADP, Gusto for driver hours and payroll integration), and Telematics (integration with existing GPS hardware providers). API documentation is available at docs.fleetnimble.com/api.

articles.title: Security & Data Protection
articles.answer: FleetNimble takes data security seriously. All data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.3 and at rest using AES-256. We are SOC 2 compliant and GDPR-ready. Customer data is isolated at the tenant level, and access is controlled through role-based permissions.
articles.details: Security measures: Data Encryption (TLS 1.3 for all API and web traffic, AES-256 for data at rest in PostgreSQL, field-level encryption for sensitive PII), Authentication (OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect, SSO support via SAML 2.0 and Azure AD, Google Workspace, Okta, multi-factor authentication available), Authorization (role-based access control with predefined roles: Admin, Manager, Dispatcher, Driver, Viewer — custom roles available on Enterprise), Compliance (SOC 2 Type II certified, GDPR compliant, data processing agreement available, data residency options in US, EU, and APAC), Infrastructure (hosted on AWS/GCP with redundant data centers, automated backups with point-in-time recovery, 99.9% uptime SLA on Enterprise plans), Monitoring (24/7 security monitoring, intrusion detection, regular penetration testing by third-party firms), and Data Retention (configurable data retention policies from 90 days to 2 years, secure data deletion process).

articles.title: Enterprise Deployment
articles.answer: FleetNimble Enterprise offers dedicated deployment options including single-tenant cloud, on-premises installation, and hybrid setups. You get a dedicated instance with your own database, custom branding, SLA guarantees, and a dedicated account manager.
articles.details: Enterprise deployment options: Single-Tenant Cloud (dedicated infrastructure in FleetNimble's AWS/GCP environment — no shared resources, isolated database and compute, custom backup schedule, enhanced SLAs), On-Premises (deployed on your own infrastructure behind your firewall — full data control, air-gapped option available for classified environments, FleetNimble provides deployment scripts and management tools), and Hybrid (core platform in cloud, sensitive data on-premises with secure sync). Features included: White-label dashboard with your branding, custom domain, dedicated support engineer, integration engineering (custom API and webhook development), custom report builder access, AI model fine-tuning options, and priority feature requests. Deployment timeline: Single-tenant cloud typically 1-2 weeks, on-premises typically 4-8 weeks depending on infrastructure readiness.

articles.title: General FAQs
articles.answer: I can answer most questions about FleetNimble features, pricing, setup, and support. Feel free to ask me about any aspect of the platform — GPS tracking, diagnostics, maintenance, drivers, fuel, reports, AI features, integrations, or anything else.
articles.details: Quick answers to common questions: Q: Do I need special hardware? A: You need an OBD-II adapter (ELM327 Bluetooth or our FleetNimble OBD Gateway) connected to each vehicle. Q: Which vehicles are compatible? A: Most vehicles made after 1996 (US) or 2001 (EU) with a standard OBD-II port. Q: Can I track vehicles in real time? A: Yes, GPS position updates every 5-30 seconds when the vehicle is active. Q: Is there a mobile app? A: Yes, FleetNimble is fully responsive and works on any device with a web browser. Native mobile apps are available for iOS and Android. Q: How long does setup take? A: You can be tracking vehicles within minutes of plugging in an OBD device and creating your account. Q: Do you offer training? A: Yes, all plans include access to our knowledge base and video tutorials. Professional and Enterprise plans include onboarding sessions.

articles.title: Mobile App FAQ
articles.answer: FleetNimble has native mobile apps for both iOS and Android available on the App Store and Google Play Store. The mobile app gives you full access to GPS tracking, vehicle status, alerts, and the AI Assistant. You can also connect OBD devices directly through your phone via Bluetooth.
articles.details: Mobile app features: Real-time GPS tracking with map view, vehicle status and diagnostics summary, push notifications for alerts, AI Assistant for voice or text queries, QR code scanning for quick OBD pairing, trip history viewing, driver scorecard access, and photo capture for vehicle inspections. The mobile app uses the same secure authentication as the web dashboard. Multi-user support allows dispatchers and managers to monitor fleet from mobile. Background location tracking is available for continuous telemetry (configurable for battery optimization). Supported on iOS 15+ and Android 11+.

articles.title: Onboarding & Getting Started
articles.answer: Welcome to FleetNimble! To get started: 1) Connect OBD devices to your vehicles from the Vehicles page, 2) Explore GPS Tracking to see your fleet on the map, 3) Check Live Diagnostics for real-time vehicle data, and 4) Visit the Dashboard for your full fleet overview. If you need a guided walkthrough, I can schedule an onboarding session with our team.
articles.details: Recommended setup sequence: Day 1 — Create your account, add vehicles (manually or bulk import via CSV), install OBD devices in vehicles, pair with FleetNimble app, verify data appears on Dashboard. Day 2-3 — Configure geofences for your operational areas, set up alert rules for speeding, geofence breaches, and critical DTC codes. Day 3-5 — Set up maintenance schedules for each vehicle (import existing service records), assign drivers to vehicles, review initial behavior data. Day 5-7 — Explore Reports, create your first scheduled report, set up AI Assistant for natural language queries, configure AI Receptionist phone number and greeting. Day 7-14 — Review first week of data, identify quick wins (fuel savings, driver coaching opportunities), schedule team training session with our onboarding specialists. Full onboarding support is included with Professional and Enterprise plans.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: Our onboarding specialists can have you fully set up and seeing ROI within the first week. Would you like me to schedule an onboarding session?

articles.title: Hardware & System Requirements
articles.answer: To use FleetNimble, you need: 1) An OBD-II adapter per vehicle (ELM327 Bluetooth or FleetNimble OBD Gateway), 2) A smartphone or tablet with Bluetooth and internet connection for data relay, 3) Internet-connected computer for the dashboard. The FleetNimble OBD Gateway can operate independently without a phone.
articles.details: Minimum requirements per vehicle: OBD-II adapter (ELM327 Bluetooth — widely available, typically $15-30 USD per unit, limited to ~10m Bluetooth range, requires phone nearby with FleetNimble app running; FleetNimble OBD Gateway — recommended, $149 per unit, integrated 4G LTE and GPS, 30m Bluetooth range, works independently without phone). For the dashboard: any modern web browser (Chrome 90+, Firefox 90+, Safari 15+, Edge 90+), internet connection (broadband recommended, works on 4G/5G). For mobile app: iOS 15+ or Android 11+, Bluetooth 4.0+ for OBD pairing, internet connection. Vehicle compatibility: OBD-II standard port (typically under dashboard, near steering column), works with petrol, diesel, hybrid, and electric vehicles. Not compatible with heavy-duty trucks using J1939 protocol without additional adapter.

articles.title: Data Retention & Privacy
articles.answer: FleetNimble stores your fleet data for as long as your account is active. Data retention periods are configurable from 90 days to 24 months depending on your plan. You can request data export or deletion at any time. We comply with GDPR and SOC 2 standards for data handling.
articles.details: Default retention periods: GPS location data — 12 months, Trip records — 24 months, Diagnostic data — 12 months, DTC codes — 24 months, Maintenance records — duration of account, Driver scores — 24 months, Alert history — 90 days, Call recordings and transcripts — 12 months (configurable). Data export: full account export available in CSV or JSON format. Data deletion: upon account closure, all data is securely deleted within 30 days. GDPR: subject access requests processed within 30 days, right to erasure supported. Privacy: FleetNimble does not sell customer data. Data is processed only for providing the fleet management service. Full privacy policy available at fleetnimble.com/privacy.

articles.title: Multi-Language Support
articles.answer: FleetNimble supports multiple languages in the AI Assistant and AI Receptionist. The dashboard interface is available in English, and the AI features can converse naturally in multiple languages including Spanish, French, German, and more.
articles.details: Supported languages: Dashboard UI (English currently, with more languages in development on Enterprise plans), AI Assistant (responds in the language you ask in — supports 50+ languages), AI Receptionist (can be configured per tenant for primary language — supports English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, and more via Gemini/OpenAI multilingual capabilities). The AI Receptionist can detect the caller's language and respond in the same language on supported providers.

articles.title: Data Backup & Recovery
articles.answer: FleetNimble performs automated backups of all customer data. Backups are taken daily with point-in-time recovery capability. Enterprise plans include custom backup schedules and dedicated disaster recovery planning.
articles.details: Backup schedule: Automated daily snapshots with 30-day retention, point-in-time recovery for last 7 days (allows restoration to any minute within 7 days), cross-region backup replication for disaster recovery (Enterprise). Recovery: Self-service restore available for Enterprise customers, FleetNimble-managed restore within 4 hours for Professional and Enterprise plans. Disaster recovery: Multi-AZ database deployment, automatic failover within 60 seconds, cross-region DR available on Enterprise with RPO of 1 hour and RTO of 4 hours.

articles.title: Uptime & SLA
articles.answer: FleetNimble offers 99.9% uptime SLA on Enterprise plans and 99.5% on Professional plans. All plans include proactive monitoring and automated failover to ensure your fleet data is always available when you need it.
articles.details: Service Level Agreements: Starter — best effort (no SLA), Professional — 99.5% monthly uptime guarantee, Enterprise — 99.9% monthly uptime guarantee. Credits for SLA breaches apply (Professional: 5% credit per 0.5% below SLA, max 25%; Enterprise: 10% credit per 0.1% below SLA, max 50%). Planned maintenance is performed during defined maintenance windows with 48-hour notice. Exclusions include force majeure, customer-side issues, and third-party service disruptions. Historical uptime: 99.97% average across all services over the past 12 months.

articles.title: AI Receptionist Call Features
articles.answer: The AI Receptionist handles incoming calls 24/7. It can greet callers with your business name, look up returning customers, book appointments, create support tickets, answer product questions, and transfer to a human when needed. You can configure business hours, custom greetings, and which features are enabled.
articles.details: Call features: Custom Greeting (configure your welcome message, business name, and tone), Business Hours (set hours when calls are handled by AI, optionally forward after-hours calls to voicemail), Caller ID Lookup (automatic identification of returning customers by phone number), Appointment Booking (step-by-step collection of caller info, conflict checking, and CRM creation), Support Ticket Creation (capture issue details, urgency, and affected vehicle), Product Q&A (answers from verified FleetNimble knowledge base), Proactive Sales (naturally mention related features based on conversation context), Human Handoff (transfer to sales, support, or emergency department), Call Notes (save conversation notes to CRM), and End Call (graceful call termination with summary). Configuration is available from Settings > AI Receptionist in the dashboard.
articles.proactiveSalesTip: The AI Receptionist also works as a pre-qualification tool. It captures lead details and scores them before a human salesperson ever picks up the phone.

articles.title: Electric Vehicle Support
articles.answer: FleetNimble supports electric vehicles with EV-specific monitoring including battery level, charging status, range estimation, and charging session tracking. All standard features like GPS tracking, diagnostics (where available), and maintenance scheduling work with EVs as well.
articles.details: EV-specific features: Battery Level Monitoring (state of charge percentage, estimated range remaining), Charging Status (charging, discharging, full, plugged in but not charging, unplugged), Charging Session Tracking (session start/end, energy added in kWh, cost if rate configured), EV Range Analytics (range per charge, efficiency in km/kWh or mi/kWh, range degradation over time), and EV-Specific Alerts (low battery, charging interrupted, unplugged vehicle). EVs are supported via OBD-II (where the vehicle exposes standard PIDs) and can also integrate with EV API services for more detailed telemetry (Enterprise plan).
